verses.1: And Jacob settled in the land of his father’s ancestors, in the land of Canaan.
verses.2: These were the sons of Jacob. Joseph was the son of seventeen years old. He took care of his brothers in the field. When he grew up, he married the daughters of Bilhah and Zilpah, his father’s sisters. Joseph brought bad news to his father.
verses.3: And Israel loved Joseph more than all his other sons. He was like a father to him, and he made a statue for him out of gold.
verses.4: And his brothers saw that they loved him more than all their other brothers. So they hated him, and they couldn’t say anything to comfort him.
verses.5: And Joseph had a dream. He told his brothers about it, and they gathered around him again.
verses.6: And he said to them, “Listen to this dream that I have had.”
verses.7: And behold, we are standing among the idols in the field. And behold, my idol has come to life; it also stands upright. And behold, your idols will be turned aside from their positions, and they will worship my idol.
verses.8: And his brothers said to him, “If you become king over us, then rule over us. They also supported him in his plans and decisions.”
verses.9: And he dreamed another dream. He told his brothers about it. He said, “Look, I’ve dreamed again. And look, there’s the sun, the moon, and eleven stars that are bowing down to me.”
verses.10: And he told his father and brothers about it. His father became angry with him and said, “What kind of dream is this that you’ve had? We will come to pay homage to you.”
verses.11: And his brothers and father were angry with him, but he kept the word to himself.
verses.12: And their brothers went to the field where their father’s sheep were grazing.
verses.13: And Israel said to Joseph, “Do you really think your brothers are good people in Shechem? I’ll send you there to deal with them.” But he replied, “Here I am.”
verses.14: And he said to him, “Please see the peace of your brothers and the peace of the sheep. Then return and tell me what happened.” So he sent him away from the edge of his camp. And Shkema came.
verses.15: And someone found him. He was lying in the field. The man asked him, “What are you doing here?”
verses.16: And he said to his brothers, “I ask you, please tell me where they are.”
verses.17: And the man said, “They have gone away from here. I heard people saying, ‘Let’s go to Dothan.’ So Yosef went with his brothers, and they found them in Dothan.”
verses.18: And they saw him from a distance, before he could come closer to them. So they ordered that he be killed.
verses.19: And they said to each other, “Look, here is the man who has these dreams.”
verses.20: And now, let’s go and kill him. Let’s throw him into one of the ditches. Then we will say, “May he suffer greatly!” We will see what his thoughts will be.
verses.21: And Reuben heard this, and he tried to get rid of him. He said, “Let us not kill him.”
verses.22: And Ravan said to them, “Do not shed blood. Throw him into this pit that is located in the harbor. Do not use your hands to harm him, so that he may be saved from your hands and returned to his father.”
verses.23: And when Joseph came to his brothers, they stripped Joseph of his coat, and also removed the symbols that were on his coat.
verses.24: And he took it, and threw it into the fire. But there was no water in it at all.
verses.25: And they sat down to eat bread. They raised their eyes and saw that the tent of Israel was coming from Gilgal. Their clothes were torn and dirty. They went away to bring them out of Egypt.
verses.26: And Yehuda said to his brothers, “What is the use of our killing our brothers and covering their bodies with our skins?”
verses.27: Go, and let us be sold to the Israelites. Let our hands not be tied in their hands, for they are our brothers through blood. May their brothers also listen to them.
verses.28: And men from Dan brought Josue down from the boat. They sold Josue to the Israelites for twenty silver coins. Then they brought Josue back from Egypt.
verses.29: And Reuben sat down in the tent. But there was no Joseph in the tent. So he tore his clothes apart.
verses.30: And he returned to his brothers and said, “The child is not mine. I am Anah. I am here.”
verses.31: They took Joseph’s coat, slaughtered a ram, and immersed the coat in the blood.
verses.32: And they sent out the writing on the tablets. They brought it back to their father, and said, “We have found this! Please, let this writing be kept in your possession.”
verses.33: And she recognized her as a poisonous creature. She said, “My son, this is a bad thing. You have eaten him; he has become a prey to others.”
verses.34: And Jacob cut his clothes and put on his sandals. He wept over his son for many days.
verses.35: And all his sons and daughters stood up to comfort him. They tried to console him, but he said, “I will go down to my children’s place.” Then his father took him away from them.
verses.36: And the merchants sold him to the Egyptians, to Potiphar Seris, the king of the Pharaohs.
